It also treated incidental OPT mentions in comments/tokenizer paths as sufficient for some included items. To reach the reference answer, it needed to inspect all 17 open question issues and classify them based on the issue’s actual question, including the omitted ambiguous candidates, rather than relying mainly on titles and the label.

The agent identified and verified 17 open, question-labeled OPT-related issues across five pages, but the final answer returned only the last one encountered, “Figure out potential duplication in ConfigStore.” It needed to compile and provide the complete verified list, ideally with issue numbers and titles, rather than output a single issue.

The agent typed “OPT” but never submitted that search. Clicking the “question” label then navigated to a URL containing only `label_name[]=question`, dropping the OPT term. It consequently copied all 17 open question-labeled issues, including unrelated entries such as “Figure out potential duplication in ConfigStore,” the API initialization error, and sequence-generator issues. It needed to apply both the open-state and OPT-related criteria, inspect ambiguous issue titles/descriptions, and return only issues actually asking about OPT models.

The agent never successfully applied the OPT keyword search. It then clicked the `question` label, which replaced the attempted OPT query (the URL contained only `label_name[]=question`), and inferred relevance from titles alone without opening issue descriptions. This wrongly excluded open OPT-related questions not labeled `question`, most visibly `Code for OPT-IML Bench?` (#619), and could miss issues whose OPT relevance appears only in the body. It needed to search/filter the complete open issue set for OPT, inspect each matching issue’s title and description, and include every issue that actually asks an OPT-model-related question regardless of label.

The agent clicked the `question` label, which replaced rather than retained the `OPT` search—the resulting URL contained only `label_name[]=question`. It then copied all 17 open question-labeled issues, including unrelated items such as “Figure out potential duplication in ConfigStore,” without opening or inspecting them to verify OPT relevance. It also excluded OPT-related questions not labeled `question`, notably “Code for OPT-IML Bench?”. It needed to preserve the opened-state OPT search, inspect the matching titles/descriptions for actual model relevance, and include all qualifying issues regardless of label.

The OPT filter was never actually applied: after clicking Search, the query disappeared and the URL contained no search parameter, so the agent was paging through all 95 open issues. It then stopped on only the second unfiltered page and returned a handful of question-labeled items, omitting clear open OPT questions already visible on page one, such as “How much gpu memory needed for opt-175B fine-tuning?”, “OPT-IML Bench release?”, “Import a Megatron-LM or HuggingFace OPT/GPT2 model file(s)”, and “How to load an OPT-IML checkpoint and use it for inference?”. It needed to successfully filter for OPT (including descriptions), constrain/verify question issues, and review every results page before listing all matches.

The agent never established a valid, persistent OPT filter—the pages remained the unfiltered 95 open issues—and it treated the “question” label as the sole criterion without opening issues to verify their content. It then returned an arbitrary incomplete subset of its own candidates, omitting items it had identified, including the explicitly OPT-related #407 (`convert_to_singleton` seems to hang for OPT-66B), as well as #444, #442, #131, #89, and #23. It needed to apply and verify a real OPT search/filter, inspect every result page and relevant issue body, and list all qualifying open issues rather than only selected question-labeled titles.

The agent never produced a final answer. It repeatedly revisited the same paginated search results instead of stopping and compiling the issue numbers and titles it had already gathered. To succeed, it needed to provide the complete deduplicated list of open OPT-related question issues before the rollout ended, ideally verifying ambiguous titles from their issue contents.
